product.title: AI Agent Runtime Authority | WhitePact Product
product.heading: Authority before action
product.description: WhitePact evaluates whether an AI-agent action is authorized before consequential execution on supported, configured paths. Explore the control, the benefit and the boundary.
sections: Evaluate a declared action

Bring identity, delegated authority, purpose and applicable policy together before a supported action proceeds. Authentication identifies a principal; it does not establish permission to perform an action.
Turn judgment into a guarded action

Evaluation output is not enforcement by itself. Consequential effects must pass through the configured guarded execution boundary. Scoped, time-bound grants apply where implemented; approval does not create authority in the browser.
Keep approval explicit

An approval-required result means the action has not executed. Authorized approvers resolve the request through the service, and the supported execution path checks current authorization before proceeding. A denied action remains denied.
Understand the outcome

Evidence records support investigation and audit. They are not authority and do not independently prove an external effect. UNKNOWN must remain UNKNOWN: reconcile the external system before any retry, even after an HTTP success or redirect.
A boundary you must configure

WhitePact does not control arbitrary code, direct tool calls outside its integration paths or compromised infrastructure. Identify the trusted computing boundary and validate the deployed configuration for each integration. Source implementation, public deployment and commercial availability are separate facts.
Sovereign

Sovereign is a distinct WhitePact product surface. Review its public product page for its current scope and prerequisites; access to a browser shell does not confer authority to its protected data or actions.

architecture.title: AI Agent Authority Boundary Architecture | WhitePact
architecture.heading: Separate thought from authority
architecture.description: Agent intent is not execution authority. Explore WhitePact's control, execution, evidence and revocation layers on supported, configured enforcement paths.
sections: The operating doctrine
The agent may think freely. It may plan freely. But it cannot act outside independently enforced authority.
Identity is not authority

A session or machine credential establishes who is asking. The configured service evaluates the action's authority, intent, consent, policy, risk and approval against current authorization state. A subscription or client-side assertion cannot substitute for those checks.
Evaluation is not enforcement

A judgment becomes operational only when the consequential effect passes through the supported guarded execution boundary. Integrators must constrain alternative paths, protect credentials and establish what code and infrastructure remain trusted.
Know the trusted boundary

Arbitrary tool or plugin code inside a trusted process and direct calls outside configured paths are not universally controlled. Isolation depends on the supported deployment configuration. A Python configuration flag does not establish an independent boundary for arbitrary code.
Trust the deployment, not just the diagram

The operator must trust the configured service code, credential handling, storage and execution adapters. Route agent calls through the supported boundary and restrict alternative access to consequential systems. An operator who intentionally supplies a direct path around WhitePact has created a bypass outside that enforcement scope.
A failed check is not permission

Authentication failure, unavailable authorization state or a denied admission must not be treated by the integrator as permission to fall back to direct execution. Dependency failure and uncertainty are operational incidents to handle explicitly. Validate each selected adapter's failure behavior; this conceptual map does not certify every deployment as fail-closed.
Failure and uncertainty

Approval-required and denied requests must not be treated as permission to execute. UNKNOWN does not prove success or failure. Missing evidence, an HTTP success or a redirect is insufficient confirmation of a downstream effect; reconcile before retrying.
Revocation has a time boundary

Revocation blocks subsequent checks on the supported path. It cannot retroactively reverse an external effect that has already completed. Grant scope, expiry and current authorization checks must be reviewed in the selected integration contract.

developers.title: Developer Entry Points | WhitePact
developers.heading: Connect the action boundary
developers.description: Start a local evaluation, connect a supported API or MCP action, and handle denial, approval and uncertainty without turning a client response into authority.
sections: Start with the CLI

The repository defines the whitepact CLI for product diagnostics and platform utilities. Start with whitepact --help and whitepact info. The documented Python distribution is rai-governance-platform; the product name is not the installation name. Optional commands have their own dependency requirements.
Before your first action

Use the pinned source quickstart in the docs, configure the supported runtime dependencies and obtain an organization-scoped machine credential with the required role. The selected tool must be registered and supported. Configure legitimate authority and consent in the backend before expecting an action to proceed; an API key alone is insufficient.
Python HTTP helpers

The source Python GovernanceRuntimeClient provides Bearer-authenticated calls for governed tools, approvals and evidence. Review its request and result contracts in the versioned source before integrating. Keep credentials in trusted server-side code.
TypeScript source SDK

The repository contains TypeScript governance helpers for tool calls, approvals and evidence. Review and build the source against the selected server contract. This page does not represent the source SDK as an available published npm package.
MCP and API

Use the configured Streamable HTTP /mcp endpoint or the governed API tool-call interface on your verified host. These integration interfaces require authentication and a registered supported tool. An anonymous documentation page does not grant access to protected integration references or API operations.
Tool discovery is not tool authority

An MCP-capable agent may discover a tool without being authorized to invoke it. Route the MCP request through the configured WhitePact authority boundary before the supported tool executes. WhitePact does not automatically govern unrelated MCP servers or a client's direct tool calls.
Handle results deliberately

An approval-required request has not executed; denial grants no authority. Preserve UNKNOWN and reconcile the downstream system before any retry. Use authenticated evidence lookup within the signed-in organization and review the generated reference for exact schemas.
Resolve, execute, inspect and revoke

Use the documented approval resolution and execution interfaces only when the current backend permits them; resolution is not a client-created grant. Inspect the supported evidence list or signed-in evidence detail. After credential or authority revocation, subsequent supported checks must use current state. Reconcile UNKNOWN before retrying: neither revocation nor a retry can undo a completed external effect.
Verify before production

Confirm the host, credential scope, registered tools, service/runtime enforcement and operational configuration. The examples and source prove implementation contracts, not that a particular hosted deployment is ready or that every integration path enforces every control.

security.title: Security Boundary | WhitePact
security.heading: Controls with a defined scope
security.description: Evaluate WhitePact security through its supported control paths, documented evidence and explicit limitations.
sections: Protect the authorization path

Human sessions and machine credentials have distinct trust paths. Authentication alone does not authorize an action. Keep API credentials server-side and validate organization scope and lifecycle behavior in the configured backend.
Constrain execution and replay

Review grant scope, expiry, approval consumption and current authorization checks in the selected runtime contract. Do not replay an uncertain operation. Revocation affects subsequent supported checks and cannot undo a completed external effect.
Tenant boundaries are deployment requirements

Authenticated access must remain organization-scoped at the server. Browser-supplied identifiers and client-side controls are not authorization. Validate the supported credential, storage and resource-access paths in the actual installation rather than inferring isolation from the website.
Failure, telemetry and incident handling

A denied or unavailable authorization check is not permission for a direct fallback. Review supported health and telemetry surfaces without treating them as security authority. Establish incident ownership, evidence retention and downstream reconciliation before operating consequential actions; this page does not promise a staffed response team or an SLA.
Tamper evidence, not an absolute ledger

Hash-chained records support detection of changes within documented verifier and storage boundaries. They are not an immutable ledger against a fully compromised database. Evidence alone does not establish authority or prove a downstream effect.
Operators remain in the boundary

Deployment security includes trusted code, infrastructure, secrets, network paths and storage. WhitePact does not claim universal enforcement over arbitrary plugins, bypass paths or compromised operators. Review the integration's trusted computing boundary before relying on a control.
Assurance status

Implemented controls, production validation and external certification are separate facts. WhitePact does not currently claim SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification, an independent commercial penetration test or an uptime guarantee. The Trust Center records the published assurance scope.
Report a vulnerability

Use the repository's coordinated disclosure policy and its published security contact for suspected vulnerabilities. Follow the policy's current reporting instructions and avoid including secrets in public issues.

enterprise.title: Enterprise Evaluation | WhitePact
enterprise.heading: Evaluate your operating boundary
enterprise.description: Assess deployment, identity lifecycle, tenant scope and evidence requirements against the configuration you intend to operate.
sections: Deployment is a responsibility

Define the supported integration paths and their trusted computing boundary. Review secrets, storage, transport, backup, recovery and isolation requirements for your environment. Repository implementation is not a claim that a hosted commercial service is available or production validated.
Identity and lifecycle

Map human and machine principals to explicit authority and organization scope. Evaluate provisioning, credential rotation, revocation and approval responsibilities against the current backend contract. A paid entitlement does not authorize agent action.
Tenant and data boundaries

Validate organization-scoped data access and the storage configuration with your own tenancy and retention requirements. Operators must verify deployment settings and access paths; a corporate page cannot establish tenant isolation for a particular installation.
Evidence and SIEM planning

Review the available evidence and incident records, their schemas and authenticated access controls against your audit workflow. Confirm the supported export or ingestion path before planning a SIEM integration. Hash-chain verification does not replace storage protection or external reconciliation.
Operational acceptance

Test denied, approval-required, expired or revoked authorization and UNKNOWN outcomes on each supported consequential path. Establish reconciliation procedures before retrying uncertain operations. Revocation cannot reverse a completed external effect.
Commercial and assurance review

Treat source implementation, deployed capability, commercial availability and external certification as separate acceptance criteria. Confirm configuration, responsibilities and any agreement directly; this page introduces no certification, staffed support or SLA commitment.
